implementation_state: Persistence and ownership exist: AppState owns an AccountStore behind the optional account feature, and the registry is configuration on ProviderConfig. Execution exists as account::reconcile, which probes declared accounts through a dyn shim and publishes into the store — including on failure, so a stale healthy reading cannot masquerade as current. Two further account-owned surfaces have since been added: a provider-neutral observation layer (ObservedResourceEvent, ResourceEffect, ObservedProviderAccounting) with a bounded AccountEventLog, and a maintenance block on AccountConfig carrying the check-in declaration. The maintenance block now has a scheduler: checkin_enabled and checkin_interval_secs are consumed by account::checkin::decide, a pure function of the declaration, the last settlement and an injected instant, and a minute timer in the desktop shell walks the declared accounts and starts the ones it calls Due. The node stays PARTIAL, and the reason is narrower than it was: the reconciler still has no call site and no credential path feeds it, and the resource-event log still has no consumer. What the scheduler deliberately does not do is guess: an account with no recorded settlement is refused as NeedsFirstObservation even when an interval is declared, because nothing is known about when a given relay's daily reset falls and opening one browser per account at launch is the failure being guarded against. The consequence is stated rather than hidden — automation begins only after a person has started one check-in per account. The settlement history is durable, because the in-memory view a panel renders is empty on every launch and reading a schedule from it would make every account look untried after every restart. See E-119, E-130, E-131, E-132, E-134. The observation layer has the same shape of gap: written, fixture-tested, and held by nothing, so no observed resource event reaches a consumer. It would be easy to read the added surface as progress toward integration and it is not; the parts are proven and the wiring is absent. The record previously claimed persistence and ownership did not exist; it corrected the record, not the code. See E-119, E-130, E-131, E-132.
required_gates: Generic account types and pure calculations
unblock_condition: Satisfied. Stage 5 is revalidated at E-133, the owned persistence and runtime contract shipped at E-119, and ML feature order is untouched: default remains ["ml"]. Why the status still does not move on that basis is stated in the notes, because it is a distinction and not a formality.
notes: Check-in is the second account-owned execution surface and the only one that can now run without a person, behind an opt-in feature. The reconciler still has no caller and the resource-event log still has no consumer; neither is wired. The scheduler has never run against a real relay console, and the interval has never elapsed against a live panel.

ALL THREE OF THIS NODE'S GATES ARE NOW MET and none of them is about integration, which is the whole reason blocked_by can be empty while the status is PARTIAL. OBSERVABILITY is the precedent for the opposite conclusion and it was not followed here, because the two cases differ in one respect that matters: observability is unreachable from the product deliberately and 7F owns its real-traffic use, whereas account::reconcile is unreachable because nothing calls it and no successor node owns that work either. A deliberate handoff is a gate satisfied; an unowned gap is not. A reader who disagrees with that reading has a reasonable case and the argument is here rather than hidden in the absence of an explanation.
